courseTitle: 100 Days of Code: JavaScript Data Structures and Algorithms

lectures.title: Why DFS does not Work for SSSPP?

cues.en: Now, we have talked about how breadth first search algorithm works for single source shortest path
problem.
Now when we talk about the graph traversal we have talked about also depth first search.
Now you might be interested that if we use the breadth first search algorithm for this problem, why
we cannot use the depth first search algorithm.
When we talk about the depth first search algorithm, we said that it continues as deep as possible.
So this means that if we start from the A, the first neighbor of A is B and the second neighbor of
A is C.
So this means that according to depth first search we are going to continue to the deepest neighbor
which is C.
So then when we come to C we are going to continue one more time to the deepest node which is d in this
case because from C we can only go to D.
Now when we come to D we are going to continue to the deepest neighbor as well.
So here again from D we can go only to E.
So we are going to continue to E.
Then from E we are going to continue to the next node which is B in this case.
Now if we look at these steps over here, you can easily see that from A to B it takes one, two, three
and four steps to reach B according to the depth first search algorithm.
But it can be easily seen that from A to B we can go directly by using the direct link, as this is
unweighted graph, so it will take only one step.
So this is a shortest path.
So this means that we cannot find the shortest path by using the depth first search algorithm.
Because depth first search algorithm continues as deep as possible.
And it is not exploring any other nodes to find out the shortest path.
So that's why we cannot solve the single source shortest path problem using depth first search algorithm.
